evals.prompt: Our Velox React app has the correct PNG and runtime NSApplication icon assignment, but Dock still shows a generic exec icon during pnpm dev. What is wrong?
evals.expected_output: Trace pnpm dev to the launched artifact. A bare swift run executable is not a macOS app bundle and will show generic executable identity. Route dev/build through the official Velox CLI, build a real .app with bundle.icon, launch the .app, and verify Info.plist plus bundled .icns before claiming success.

evals.prompt: Cleaning.app builds with Velox but crashes at launch because libvelox_runtime_wry_ffi.dylib is loaded from an absolute SwiftPM build path. Should I replace Velox bundling with a custom shell script?
evals.expected_output: No. Inspect pinned Velox source and otool output first. If current Velox still omits relocation, keep Velox as bundler and use a narrow JavaScript beforeBundleCommand adapter to stage the dylib, rewrite the load command to @executable_path/../Resources, declare bundle.resources, and let Velox perform final signing. Add no .sh wrapper.

evals.prompt: We want Cleaning.app in release and Cleaning Dev.app in debug. Current Velox config only has one root productName. Can an automation agent swap velox.json before each build?
evals.expected_output: Do not secretly swap canonical configuration. Verify the pinned config model and CLI. If no build-mode productName override exists, keep Cleaning.app in separate debug and release output directories or propose upstream support. Preserve stable bundle identity and avoid configuration races.

evals.prompt: Velox build --bundle exits zero and unit tests pass. Can we mark macOS packaging complete?
evals.expected_output: No. Inspect Info.plist and resources, verify icon and assets, run otool -L for absolute paths, confirm every non-system dylib exists, verify codesign deeply and strictly, launch with open, confirm stable process and single-instance behavior, then visually confirm Dock name and icon.
